subject: Clarification: model training exclusion & prompt/response rights
messages:
From: Lara Schmidt <lara@medsyn.com>
To: mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: legal@medsyn.com
Date: 2027-02-14T09:12:00Z
Subject: Clarify model training exclusion and prompt/response rights

Hi Mateo / Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — impressed by the throughput and the observability dashboard. Before we move deeper on procurement, our legal and privacy teams need to lock down a few items in the DPA and SOW related to AI data use:

1) No-training commitment: we need contractual assurance that customer prompts and model outputs will not be used to improve any public or internal model weights or training corpora. Please confirm what options you offer (default behaviour vs paid add-on) and how this is enforced technically.

2) Prompt / response ownership: MedSyn needs explicit language stating that prompts and generated outputs are customer IP and may not be used by Redwood for any derivative works.

3) Subprocessors & transfers: provide your EU-residency options and a current list of subprocessors. We are particularly concerned about any offshore log processing.

4) Evidence & verification: our auditors will want an evidence pack showing logs, retention timelines, and the process for verifying no-training (eg. audit trails, sysadmin access policies).

I've attached our initial redline of your standard DPA (MedSyn-DPA-redline.pdf). Oliver from MedSyn legal is looped in. Can you confirm whether the wording below is achievable? If not, please propose alternative language and the operational controls you will apply.

- Lara
Lara Schmidt
Director of Product Risk, MedSyn Health

Attachments: MedSyn-DPA-redline.pdf

From: mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai
To: Lara Schmidt <lara@medsyn.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, dev_patel@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-02-15T10:04:00Z
Subject: Re: Clarify model training exclusion and prompt/response rights

Hi Lara — thanks for the clear write-up and the redline. Looping in Dev and Karthik so we can give a combined legal+technical response. Short answer up front: yes — we can contractually offer a "no-training" option and explicit output ownership language. Below are the practical details and choices for MedSyn to consider.

What we offer (options):
- No-training contractual addendum (no customer prompt/response used for model training, weight updates, or public benchmarking). This is available as a standard addendum for enterprise DPAs.
- Ephemeral caching: by default we maintain short-term in-memory KV caches to support multi-turn context; we can configure retention policies and opt to not persist logs to long-term storage for no-train customers.
- Output ownership: we are prepared to add explicit language that customer prompts and generated outputs are the customer's IP and Redwood will not assert derivative rights.
- Evidence portal & attestation: we provide an evidence pack (retention screenshots, access logs, subprocessor list) and a quarterly attestation for enterprise agreements.

Operational controls (how we enforce no-train):
- Isolation: no-train customers are put into a logical tenancy flag that disables pipeline steps that would otherwise sample requests into internal improvement queues.
- Logging: telemetry required for operational health is minimized and can be redacted; optional telemetry for quality is explicitly excluded unless turned on by you.
- Subprocessors: we offer EU-resident processing paths (AWS eu-west-1, GCP europe-west). We maintain a current subprocessor registry and can provide SOC2 reports and pubkeys for audit.

Can you confirm which of the above you need (1) strict no-train + EU-only processing + quarterly attestation, or (2) no-train + limited EU residency (some logs in us for monitoring) + annual attestation? Once you confirm, Karthik will propose precise contract language.

Best,
Mateo Alvarez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Thanks — a couple of clarifications from the MedSyn legal side:

1) We appreciate the tenancy flag approach. We want the DPA to expressly prohibit use of customer data for internal model evaluation unless we give written consent. Narrow carve-outs for telemetry should be limited, logged, and subject to anonymization.

2) Subprocessors: please provide a machine-readable current list and a commitment to notify us 30 days before adding any new subprocessor that will access customer prompts or outputs.

3) Audit rights: we need the right to receive evidence and — in the event of dispute — to engage an independent auditor (redwood covers reasonable costs).

Attached: redline-with-comments.docx (we added inline suggested edits). Can you have Karthik propose contractual text for the no-training addendum and the 30-day subprocessor notice? Also confirm whether Redwood will commit to EU residency for processing of prompts and stored outputs.

Subject: Re: Clarify model training exclusion and prompt/response rights — technical evidence

Hi Oliver / team — quick technical note to back up Mateo's operational summary and to provide the evidence items you requested.

1) EU processing path: we can guarantee request routing to eu-west-1 regions for all production traffic when you select the EU residency option. We use region pinning at the load-balancer and routing policy layer.

2) Persistence & retention: for no-train customers we can disable long-term persistence for prompts/outputs. Short-lived KV cache remains in RAM for active sessions only and is purged immediately on session end; optionally we can set a 0-day retention policy for persistent logs.

3) Subprocessor matrix: attached is the current snapshot of subprocessors (subprocessor-matrix.csv). We also publish updates to a restricted Drive link; we'll add MedSyn to that ACL and commit to 30-day notice for changes that impact prompt/output access.

4) Evidence pack: sample report attached (evidence-pack-summary.pdf) shows retention screenshots, access logs (redacted), and the current attestation template we use for quarterly reports. We cannot divulge host-level keys but we can provide SOC2 Type II and enable a limited technical audit under NDA.

Let me know if you want a short technical walkthrough (30 min) for your security team.

— Dev Patel
Principal Systems Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: subprocessor-matrix.csv, evidence-pack-summary.pdf

Hi Lara / Oliver — appreciate the quick back-and-forth. Recap & proposed mutual action plan so we can get this into contracting: 

Agreed points:
- Redwood will provide a "No-Training" contractual addendum that prevents use of MedSyn prompts/outputs for model training or model improvement unless MedSyn provides prior written consent.
- Prompts and generated outputs will be defined as customer IP; Redwood will not assert derivative rights.
- MedSyn will be added to our restricted Drive ACL for a live subprocessor registry and will receive 30 days' notice before any change to subprocessors that may access prompts/outputs.
- Evidence pack & quarterly attestation will be provided; SOC2 Type II report will be shared under NDA.

Next steps:
1) Karthik will circulate precise redline language for the DPA addendum by EOD Wednesday (2027-02-23).
2) Legal teams exchange a final DPA redline and sign; Redwood will attach the no-train addendum to the Master Services Agreement.
3) Dev to schedule a 30-min technical walkthrough for MedSyn security (suggested slot: 2027-02-24).
4) Once signed, Redwood will enable EU-residency routing and set the retention flags per the addendum.

If that all sounds right, please confirm and we'll escalate to our contracts team. Happy to provision the attestation sample now so your auditors can review.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
